pages.text: "Mom, look at that butterfly!" The herd walked in a line across the grassland. A yellow butterfly fluttered before Moya's nose. "I want to catch it!"
It fluttered into the tall grass. Moya slipped away from Mom and chased. "Just a little farther!" As Moya followed, the herd's hoofbeats faded.
The butterfly escaped. Moya turned—where was Mom? Where was the herd? Tall grass crowded every side. Their heart thumped and their ears flattened backward.
Just as tears came, Moya remembered Mom's words. "If you can't see me, stop where you are!" Moya stopped instead of running about, and took a big breath. "I can do this."
Looking around, Moya saw Nia's head above the grass. Mom had said, "Find a grown-up or friend you know and stay beside them." Moya walked toward Nia.
"Nia, I've lost Mom. She calls the loudest whinny." Nia lowered their neck to meet Moya's eyes. "You did well. Let's find her. Then stay close to Mom." Moya sniffled. "Stay close to Mom!"
Nia raised their neck and called across the grass. "Moya's mom! Moya's here!" Moya stood close to Nia's legs and called, too. Now it wasn't scary. They only had to wait.
Far away, the grass parted. Mom came running. "Moya!" "Mom!" Moya hurried over and laid their neck across hers. Mom nuzzled their back.

Mom walked with Moya close beside her. "You stopped and waited with Nia. So brave!" Moya knew the steps. "One, stop if I can't see Mom! Two, stay beside a friend I know! Three, call Mom loudly!" Nia waved their neck goodbye.

Back in the herd, Mom held Moya close against her side and nuzzled them. "Stay close to Mom!" Even when Mom disappeared, stopping and calling had brought them together again. Moya walked softly beside her.
